question: Each of P, Q, R, S, T, U and V has an exam on a different day of a week starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week. U has an exam on Saturday. Only 4 people have an exam between S and T, neither of whom has an exam on Monday. P has an exam immediately after R, and V has an exam immediately before R. T has an exam after P. How many people have an exam after S?
solution:
**Given :** Each of P, Q, R, S, T, U and V has an exam on a different day of a week starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week.

1) U has an exam on Saturday.

2) Only 4 people have an exam between S and T, neither of whom has an exam on Monday.

For there to be 4 people between S and T, they must be at the two ends of the week. Since neither can be on Monday, this means one must be on Tuesday and the other on Sunday.

3) P has an exam immediately after R, and V has an exam immediately before R.

This forms a consecutive block: V-R-P. This block requires three consecutive empty slots.

4) T has an exam after P.

Let's consider the two cases for S and T:

In both cases, the three consecutive empty slots for the V-R-P block are Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. Thus, V is on Wednesday, R is on Thursday, and P is on Friday.

Case 1 (T on Sunday): P is on Friday and T is on Sunday. T has an exam after P. This matches the condition. Thus, Case 1 is Valid.

Case 2 (T on Tuesday): P is on Friday and T is on Tuesday. T has an exam before P, which contradicts the condition that T has an exam after P.

Thus, Case 2 is Eliminated.

The final arrangement is based on Case 1. The only remaining person is Q, and the only remaining empty slot is Monday.
